title: Duplex Forgery Proof–Attack Gap
summary: Generic Duplex analyses use a data–time boundary exponential in c, but the best-known forgery attack applies only at a scale exponential in three-halves c; closing the gap remains open.

formal_statement.body: For generic Duplex-based authenticated-encryption constructions with data--time product $DT$ and capacity parameter $c$, find a forgery attack matching the security-analysis boundary associated with $DT \ll 2^c$, or improve the best-known attack, which applies only in the regime $DT \gg 2^{3c/2}$, enough to close this proof--attack gap.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of generic Duplex-based authenticated-encryption constructions.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find a forgery attack matching the analysis boundary associated with DT ≪ 2^c, or improve the attack known only for DT ≫ 2^(3c/2), thereby closing the proof–attack gap.

progress.summary: The source states that no forgery attack matches the generic Duplex analysis boundary and places the best-known attack only in the larger data–time regime. It thus presents a concrete proof–attack gap.
citation_labels: Bishwajit Chakraborty et al., Exact Security Analysis of ASCON
